items.text: This may be the most anticipated update for JDM we have ever done, as it was the last remaining part of the whole JDM culture representation in the game that we were still missing. It took us far longer to create than we wanted to, but finally it’s here and ready for your creativity to explode!

notes.title: In November, we drift in style!

items.text: Long story short - we’ve expanded the Paint Shop experience with additional ways you can paint your car, added rim painting and the whole livery/decals systems, so you can drive on Guntama streets in a car from your dreams.
Added the livery option in the Paint Shop menu screen
Choose from hundreds of decals and stickers to create your livery.
Up to 5000 layers of stickers available at your disposal.
Full control over the process: scale, rotate, colour, symmetry mode and various camera precision settings for a robust and pleasant user experience.
Control over colour saturation, brightness and gradients.
Ability to reorder, hide and duplicate layers.
Saving liveries as presets - this also creates a separate save file in the game’s folder for each preset created.
Livery sharing in multiplayer - just drive to and inspect a player in multiplayer to save their active livery to your own library of livery presets.

Material selection - factory finish, gloss, metallic, sateen, matt, chrome
Control over colour saturation and brightness.

releases.displayName: The Expanded Paint Shop Update is just days away from going live!

items.text: It may have taken more time than we initially predicted, however the livery system is almost here! You’ve been asking for it without end from the game’s release back in 2025 and we were laser focused on providing it, as we ourselves thought the game was incomplete without it. Wanting to deliver and actually shipping a feature are two different beasts though.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/7e02d3ec3a79e8eab9d32b28bc9fb0163b17449d.png"]

During the past year we have scrapped the livery system twice, each time starting the work from the beginning. There were various reasons for it - performance impact, unforeseen bugs, limits we had to put in place that made this game mechanic too shallow and in effect not really fun.

What’s really important to understand is that JDM’s focus from its conception was on car parts - the ability to switch hoods, sideskirts, whole body kits - it’s a lot of moving parts that change how the car looks, how big and wide it is, and even the biggest AAA titles, that we compete with for your attention, very often lack this diversity. You can either have car parts or you can have liveries. Having both is a tremendous challenge.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/a4574e19146217ad1bc6d3c1c681788a1f0938cd.png"]
After months of work, redesigns and taking new approaches we are finally at the finish line. The expanded paint shop is almost here and is undergoing the last polishing touches right now.

An honest disclaimer here - we did everything in our power to provide the best possible quality of it, however we do expect you folks to find small issues here and there, we also see ways to further improve the feature. We hope this update brings back a lot of players back to the game and if the interest remains high, we will be able to continue working on and expanding it even further.
The Car Painter has received a slight visual update for easier control on gamepads.

notes.title: We’ve also expanded what you can do in the shop

items.text: You can now paint rims.
Single-piece, and three-piece rims can now be painted similarly as you colour the car’s body. Stock rims will remain stock and you won’t be able to change them.
We’ve added gradients.

You can now set up a starting colour and an end colour to create a unique paint job on your car. You will also be able to manipulate the angle and position of the gradient, as well as control the saturation and brightness of them for a one-of-a-kind style that you’re looking for.
Liveries
We’ve added a new section to the Paint Shop screen - Liveries.
Here you can create your custom work of art that will go directly on your car.

We’ve set the cap to 5000 layers of stickers and decals that you can put on your favourite ride. We hope this is more than plenty for you to go on. There are a plethora of different designs: from basic primitive shapes, to patterns and logos to choose from.

Each sticker can be scaled, rotated, expanded on both the X and Y axis. You can enable symmetry, flip the decal and select whether you want the sticker to go on windows or not. The stickers have all of the gradient options as the car painting tool - meaning you can create double-coloured designs if you want to.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44021335/40d14607bab902067cf105e58dd6ff5f355bb92a.png"]
Each sticker saves as a layer, and you can freely move them around - move them to the front or back, depending on what you want to achieve.

Once your masterpiece is created you can save it as a preset - it creates a separate save file on your drive. You can also “steal” other people’s designs directly in a multiplayer session - just inspect another player in-game and copy his currently used design, it will wait for you as a preset in the paint shop.

Note that all designs are created for the specific car you drive - meaning the exact car model and the parts currently put on it. You can apply a livery for a different setup, for as long as it is the same car model, but expect the livery to not adjust automatically. You may need to tinker with the design a bit to adapt it to your own setup, if you drive with a different bumper, hood or any other part.
Launch of the Expanded Paint Shop

At the time of writing this devlog we’re looking to launch the new update at the very end of this week. The patch is right now in certification for consoles, and for now we expect the update to launch simultaneously on all platforms. If anything changes, we’ll be informing you all through our Discord channel and social media, so please follow us for all the latest!
Oh, and for those of you with a competitive spirit - we’re planning to launch a contest for the best livery when the update goes live!

We’ve got some nifty updates for you today, however before we dive into the details we wanted to say a few words.

Thank you folks for staying with us and continuing to play the game! As a small, around 30 people strong studio, we truly appreciate your ongoing support and your patience for the changes to roll out! We’re working as fast as we can but we will never be able to compete with upcoming content on the same level as some of the AAA games that you came to love. We can only promise that we’re giving everything that we have for JDM and we hope to continue seeing you on Guntama roads in the months and years ahead.

We know we have been less vocal recently but that doesn't mean that we are not constantly looking into your feedback and reading your requests. We know you want more JDM cars, we know you want some physics changes, we know you want liveries and better steering wheel support. That’s our mutual desire. JDM has been, is, and will be first and foremost a passion project for us that we want to continue evolving and pushing forward.

We’ve just released multiplayer for consoles and we’re finishing up our work on the liveries system - the two biggest features we had planned for JDM for this year. In the near future we have some surprises lined up for you that we haven’t even teased yet (and we won’t do it today), but believe us when we say that there’s some exciting news on the horizon.

For now we’re slowly looking into fixing some long standing bugs and trying to improve the game in areas we feel need most love at the moment. Not all changes will directly be felt by you but they are happening and improving the project with every update.
Once again, thank you for being with us! And now, let’s look into today’s change list (coming to all platforms simultaneously).
GAME PHYSICS

We’ve dived a little deeper into the game’s physics. The changes today are meant to improve the overall feeling of the car in-game. They are specifically aimed at enhancing the work of the suspension. We’ve improved how the force is applied to a wheel in a skid and how it translates to the suspension, correcting the reaction times for turning and recovering grip. We’ve looked into suspension rebound speeds that will help with driving on uneven surfaces. We’ve improved how the car behaves when doing small wheel corrections, especially in cars with heavy rears. All these changes should result in a more immersive experience while driving, improving the car’s handling. The changes will be felt on all devices but will be most beneficial for players’ using steering wheels.
We’ve also brought back tire pressure settings in the Car Tuning Workshop. Sorry for the recent mess-up with this!

releases.displayName: JDM’s Console Multiplayer Update is live!

items.text: The long awaited multiplayer update is live now for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S!

The multiplayer update brings all of the features previously launched on PC, including open world freeroaming and various competitive events. The update also launches with a full cross platform connectivity, allowing all JDM fans to play together regardless of their platform of choice!
Console Multiplayer Game Features

Players on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S will now be able to join open lobbies or create private rooms for up to 8 players. There are two ways to initiate a multiplayer session: select a race directly from the Main menu of the game, or hop in through the in-game smartphone option.

While in a multiplayer session, players will see new events on the world map. Driving to one will begin a vote for all of the players in the room to opt in. These races are primarily divided into grip (first on the finish line wins) and drift races (the player who scores most points wins).
Players will also be able to commence one-on-one touge challenges when inspecting other player profiles in the open world.
The 15 events already available for PC are expanded with the addition of the Tofuna Downhill and Uphill races, increasing the number of events to 17. This update also rolls out for PC players.

Based on your feedback we have rebalanced the economy in the game. We’ve increased money rewards by 30% gained by completing any single player or multiplayer event. We’ve also doubled the EXP rewards counting towards car and player reputations. The changes made are meant to hasten the process of obtaining new cars and unlocking tuning options, reducing the necessary grind to experience different cars and their potential setups.

Alongside this update we’re also launching a new free car, the FSO Polonez. A Polish classic and a truly unique mark on Polish automotive history. It’s our homage to the car and a way to preserve the memory of it in the global culture.
It launches today on all platforms and will come with three very distinct body kits: the rally variant, the bousouzoku variant and the “barnyard tuning” aesthetics variant.

items.text: After weeks of testing we’re happy to inform that the long awaited multiplayer update for JDM: Japanese Drift Master is coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on September 16!

Console players will now be able to form parties of up to 8 players in the lobby and enjoy the full cross platform connectivity between consoles and PC, bringing JDM fans closer together regardless of their device of choice.

Similar to the current PC version of the game, players will have the full open world at their disposal, where they can show off their cars and cruise around the fictional prefecture of Guntama. There are also 15 events awaiting more competitive play, beginning with grip and drift races and ending with 1 vs. 1 touge challenges.
With this update we are also introducing 2 new touge challenges for both PC and console players alike: the Tofuna Downhill and Uphill grip races.

Alongside the multiplayer update, we’re introducing an economy rebalance to the game, increasing the money rewards gained from any source by roughly 30 percent and doubling the reputation with each completed activity. The changes are meant to speed up the process of obtaining new cars and unlocking new parts for tuning experimentation.
The new economy system will launch across all platforms with this update.

Last but not least, the game’s roster will expand with the free addition of the legendary Polish car - FSO Polonez. It might not be a JDM car, however its importance for Polish culture may be as big as the AE86 was for Japan. The legacy of Polonez lives to this day and as a way to prolong its heritage and pay homage to its classic status, we’re bringing it to the game alongside three very distinct body kits representing the diverse faces the car took in its primetime.
You can read up more on the car in our previous DEVLOG.

The next step for the team is to bring the livery system to the game, finally allowing you to create unique designs that will make you stand out from the crowd. The system is still under development, but it’s rapidly nearing completion and we will have more information on its details very soon!

notes.title: Shortened loading times - event soft restarts

items.text: The loading times for repeating a mission (whether you lost it or just hit that restart button in the pause menu) have been drastically reduced. Re-loading an event should take no longer than just a couple of seconds now.
Note that loading the event for the first time will still need to load up all of the assets and it has not been influenced by this change.

notes.title: New Villain Side Story Campaign - Honey Badger

It's been just over a week since the launch of our biggest update yet - Patch 1.7.0 - and we’re keeping the momentum going! Over the past few days, we’ve been listening closely to your feedback, reports, and suggestions for further tweaks and improvements. Today’s update is the result of that collaboration, focusing mainly on enhancing gameplay, improving stability, and refining key details in our game.

Patch 1.7.1 addresses several issues reported to us by the community to deliver a smoother and more enjoyable experience. From fixing bugs in Tiger events to improving the manga reading assistant and resolving crashes related to steering wheel inputs, we’ve worked to elevate your gameplay.

While today's patch brings a noticeable upgrade, it’s just a pit stop on the road to even bigger novelties and cool features. We know many of you are excited about the upcoming liveries and decals system that will let you personalize your cars even further, and we’ll be ready to share more details - and a date - very soon. Don’t worry, you won’t have to wait long.
Below, you’ll find the detailed changes introduced in this update. Thank you for your continued support and feedback, which help us improve the game!

Fixed a bug where the AI crossed the finish line in the last Tiger campaign event.

Addressed general issues that were causing crashes.

[p align="justify"]Oh boy, this is definitely the biggest update we have introduced to the game so far. A lot of smaller and bigger changes, a multitude of community requests coming to life and new features that we promised in our roadmap. And bug fixes, a lot of bug fixes.
[p align="justify"]Hopefully everyone will find something that they were waiting for here. Let’s Drift!

[p align="justify"]Introducing the R35 EBA, a car considered by many as the ‘final form’ of the GTR series. It comes with six bodykits available to be unlocked and costs 4,900,000Y to buy at the dealer. The stock version expands the roster of our grip cars.

[p align="justify"]Hakome Stadium - a sports arena made into an ultimate race challenge; Takekaze Tōge - a racing track located at the foot of the volcano, hidden within a bamboo forest. You will find both by looking for a trophy cup marker on the map - for the former it’s Ichikara East, for the latter - northern-west side of the volcano. Available from the open world or the Challenge Mode in the Main Menu.

[p align="justify"]Following the path set by the “Rise of the Scorpion” update, which expands the plotline through opponents’ backstories, a new side story campaign is introduced to the game. The Tiger’s campaign follows the tale of Naoto Date - one of the players’ major opponents in JDM, from his childhood dream, through tragedy to a second chance at life. The campaign consists of 9 events, summing to 11 completely new races. After completing Chapter 02, Mission 01 the first part of his campaign will be marked on the map. Completing the whole campaign will reward you with Tiger’s boss car (known from the main campaign).

[p align="justify"]An expanded feature for the already existing Car Setup in the game, allowing for the modification of wheels and rims. This feature will allow players to further visually tune their cars to their hearts’ content. There are up to 7 new settings, depending on the wheel selection, available to modify. The options include rim diameter and width adjustments, as well as offset options. You will be able to change the tire profile between low, medium and high, change the tires’ width and modify spacers. Finally, you will be able to alter the rim lip type. The changes are cosmetic only, so feel free to experiment!

[p align="justify"]JDM is now running XeSS 2.1.1.1, including Frame Generation and Low Latency technology. Its implementation vastly improves performance on Intel and AMD cards and has been set as default for the owners of said GPUs.
[p align="justify"]The game now supports Multi Frame Generation times 2 and times 3 for Nvidia RTX 5xxx owners. This feature can be turned off (default) and on from the game’s graphics options menu.

[p align="justify"]We are still exploring ways to further decrease the loading times across the entire game but today we have a first batch of changes. Through various optimization processes done across the entire game the loading times should be a little shorter. We have completely removed loading screens when accessing Shops available from the Main Menu of the game - Change Car, Tuning Shop, Car Setup.
[p align="justify"]With the amount of changes made to the graphics engine the game may want to redo the Automatic Graphics Settings Configuration on launch.

[p align="justify"]We improved the general performance on handheld devices; we improved the UI positioning; we added dedicated graphical presets and balanced the visual optimization. Handheld users, please let us know how the changes improved your performance.
[p align="justify"]Mesh optimization for improved performance.
[p align="justify"]Level streaming improvements.
[p align="justify"]Reduced the memory usage in the most demanding areas of the open world.
[p align="justify"]A side note here, for all players - please remember to always have the latest drivers for your GPUs !
You will now see the weather conditions for the race ahead of you. It’s communicated through the pop-up screen when driving into the side mission’s marker in the open world.
We’ve balanced the races in rainy conditions.

We have removed the Delivery Laurel from side missions (you will still use it in campaign missions), you will now deliver the packages in the car you were driving when interacting with the side mission marker in the open world.
We have fixed the issues with the infamous Kaguchi Valley and Inadani Village landmarks. They should now properly register when taking a photo in their respective spots.
Balanced the Arcade physics model.
Improved FWD (Front Wheel Drive) car physics.
Improved AWD (All Wheel Drive) car physics.
Improved collision and force compensation physics.
[p align="justify"]Resolved physics issues causing undesirable outcomes and unbalanced forces acting on the cars.
\ Added a new sound effect when the car lands on the ground after a jump.
\[level design] Added a new, short road towards the volcano, which leads to the Takekaze Tōge race track.
\ Fixed two items in the smartphone.
\ Car telemetry now displays proper values.

\ fixed A LOT of bugs connected with car models and car parts. Mentioning every single change here would bore you to death, so please, after the update if you see an issue connected to a car or one of its modifications that has not been fixed, give us a holler.
We’ll make one single exception here, as it was a very commonly requested fix: issues connected with the Yotsuhoshi Revolution have been solved.
\ Fixed an issue where, in some instances, resetting the car back on the road would blast the car away.
\ Fixed issues, which were causing the game to crash. Minimised the probability of such issues to reappear.
\ Fixed an issue where the smartphone would react to the default input press, even if the key was rebound.
\ The navigation will no longer readjust its path to the Tuner Shop after the “New parts are available” prompt on the screen.
\ The UI will no longer disappear, if the player opens the map right before a race starts.
\ Some on-screen text and notifications have been fixed or adjusted to better reflect the situation in the game.
This wraps-up the patch notes for September.
We hope these changes will drastically improve your experience while playing JDM.
As always, if you encounter any new bugs and issues, please report them to us through our customer service tickets, which can be accessed HERE.
[p align="justify"]We’re continuing to work on promised features. The next big thing ahead is the Car Livery system.
[p align="justify"]If you have any questions or just want to chat about cars and games, you can find us, and other like-minded people, on our Discord server.

We have been teasing the upcoming changes to the game throughout the entirety of last week and now it's time to launch them live!

The scope of this update is based on your feedback and covers some of the items that received the most constructive criticism since the game launched in late May. Expect better car handling in both Arcade and Simcade physics models, as well as drastically improved driving experience when playing on a steering wheel. Force Feedback support has been revamped with additional settings and calibrations. We’ve also improved gravity physics for the game, as well as braking power, suspension work and tire grip.
We’re also introducing a new car to the fleet - Honda NSX NA1, and a completely new location - a multi story garage, which also serves as the location for a new Underground Side mission.
If you want a deep dive into some of the above topics, check out the AI devlog & the Physics 2.0 devlog.
We’ve revamped the overall physics in the game focusing on car suspension, brakes and tires, to improve the overall driving experience across both physics models.
We’ve completely reworked the Force Feedback system, to greatly improve handling the game on a steering wheel.
Improved the auto flip physics behavior.
Reworked car airborne physics. The car will now have more weight when airborne. Added cinematic cameras to big jumps.
Improved the grip parameters across the whole game in both Arcade and in Simcade physics models.
Improved gravity physics. The cars will now have more weight and more realistic physics when colliding with other objects.

These are the initial global changes we've already implemented alongside the bigger Physics 2.0 update. However, our plan is to continue working on this aspect in the following weeks, expanding it with a proper collisions system for each car.
Improved braking power for all cars (noticeable in Simcade, heavily adjusted in Arcade).

Our next step for this process is to expand the supported wheel presets with premade FFB settings presets. We estimate that by the end of summer the full list of currently supported steering wheels will receive a preset update for FFB.
AI Improvements
We’ve improved AI across traffic and opponent behaviour.

Traffic cars are now smarter - they are more mindful about the player’s position and speed and react more accordingly. We’ve targeted two main aspects of their behaviour: highways - they will now be less inclined to change lanes and move out of the player’s way, unless they are driving at high speed directly behind them. They will also change lanes more frequently, forcing the player to be more mindful when speeding on the freeways; tight, mountain roads - the traffic should now be less congested in those areas and the cars will no longer drive immediately one behind the other, leaving space for the player to manoeuvre between them.
Opponents - they are also now smarter and will actively seek the best possible route to take to win the race. They will also be more mindful about other cars, including the player, when driving.
Improved AI opponent drift interactions.
Balanced the routes that opponents take during events

Summer is upon us, but it hasn’t slowed us down. Today we have a major patch for you, which brings some serious updates to the game. We’ve already teased the return of Scorpion and here it is - a whole new (technically speaking - brought back) side story campaign about the drifting beginnings of Hatori “Scorpion” Hasashi. If you want to learn more about the new content, go HERE.

We also have some very avidly requested features making their way into the game: Photomode, anyone? It’s packed with camera settings, filters and is available at the push of that smartphone button. Have fun!

To make this addition even more entertaining, we’ve prepared a new activity - Landmarks. Look for landmark spots in the open world, take a picture there and earn a beefy sum of reputation for your car.

On the technical side of things, we’re finally bringing FSR support, which comes alongside adjustments for the rest of the upscalers, frame generation tweaks and some improvements for the graphical settings autodetection.
We’ve added HDR support and further improved performance in various regions of the map.
Oh! and there’s a new car waiting for you at the Car Dealer - Subaru Impreza GR STI.
More cars are on their way and we’re carefully looking at your favourite suggestions as we move forward with upcoming car content, so please be patient as we cook.
All these new features are launching alongside one of the biggest sales on Steam. We’re cutting the price of JDM by 25%, so it's a perfect opportunity for you to hop in and enjoy the game!
Before we move to the full patch notes, we wanted to celebrate the coming of summer with you, with a fresh new trailer, enjoy!
Added Photomode to the game.

To enter the Photomode, open the Smartphone and select Photomode. In the Photomode you will have full free camera movement as well as a plethora of options to choose from to make the best possible shot. Have fun!
Added the FSR upscaler support.
For the time being it doesn't yet support Frame Generation, but we are working on it!
Introduced some improvements for all upscalers, as well as their compatibility with various hardware. Upscalers also received a new profile "Quality Plus".
Introduced some improvements for Frame Generation settings.
The Frame Generation systems which are supported by your hardware will now be clearly communicated to you (will not be grayed out). Frame Generation has been disabled in the Main Menu screens.
Improved the gamepad input system recognition.

A proper button mapping for Xbox as well as PlayStation gamepads should now be properly recognized by the game. Please be aware that the Steam Input should be turned off in Steam settings. You can also change the button icons from the Gameplay Menu Options > Icon Set.
Added a basic anti-cheat function.
Added a simple score filter to the Challenge Mode to automatically delete unobtainable and unrealistic scores. This is only the beginning of our fight with cheaters.
Added native HDR support.
You will find a new toggle in the Graphics menu allowing you to turn HDR on. To adjust the details go to the Adjust Brightness menu afterwards.
Improved the autodetection of graphical settings.
Added the Rise of the Scorpion side missions campaign,

After completing Chapter 01, Mission 05 a new Scorpion marker will show up on the map, which will initiate the Side Story campaign. There are 8 missions in total to beat. If completed, rewards you with the Scorpion's tuned Nissan Z33 (livery included).
Added Car Setup Profiles.

When entering the Car Setup menu you will now see three predefined setups for your active car, for Drift, Grip and Stock settings. If you want to manually change the settings you can pick Custom Settings and modify your car in the same way as you could before.
Added a new Landmarks Activity for the game.

items.text: As the year comes to a close, we wanted to provide a small summary of what you might expect in the full version of the game, which will be released in Spring 2025.

Your feedback, comments, and DMs since the launch of JDM: Rise of the Scorpion was an immense help to our development process. We hear what you are saying and we know there’s still a lot we can improve before the game releases. To highlight a few aspects that are at the top of our priorities:

Performance - our goal is to have the game running smoothly even on weaker GPUs or perform better on mid and high end GPUs. We’re actively improving game streaming, as well as lighting, shadows and… well basically all aspects of the game, so you can enjoy JDM on the PCs you already own.

Input devices - steering wheels, pedal panels, handbrakes and shifters - we’re systematically adding support for additional devices and testing them in-house to be sure everything is ready for launch. That includes hardware dedicated strictly for sim racers, as well as mainstream devices you can find in electronic stores across the globe and even cheap stuff you can get online with little to no branding on them. Of course, we won’t be able to cover every single device available out there and check every single combination of devices, e.g. Logitech steering wheel, paired up with a Thrustmaster handbrake and a Moza shifter, so our robust key binding system will make a reappearance. It will be updated and will contain more settings so that with a little bit of time you will be able to bind anything to play JDM with.

Racing games rarely have an engaging plotline assigned to them. With a game inspired by Japan and its culture, it felt almost obligatory to implement manga into the gameplay. And so we did! With a full team of manga artists in-house we’re drawing the story page by page, all of which will tie to every single story event that you will encounter in the game.

Each story event will push the manga forward and at any time you will be able to read the unlocked pages via your smartphone, a feature you could already see in our prologue-demo JDM: Rise of the Scorpion.

JDM: Rise of the Scorpion introduced a prequel story to the game, which you won’t find in the full game. It’s set a few years earlier and introduces some important characters that will shape the story of JDM. The prologue is free to play, so if you haven’t done so already, you might want to check it out.

Our fictional prefecture - Guntama - will see a lot of racing very soon. You will meet colorful characters, some of them will become your friends, others fierce rivals. Expect a lot of action, drama and even some romance. We’ll get back to you with more details, early next year!

When we started the development of JDM: Japanese Drift Master we had one goal in mind - recreating Japan as precisely as it was possible. Starting with the architecture and surrounding nature and ending with the roads you will drive on. Let’s stop here for a second and talk about the latter.

If you’ve played enough racing games in your life, you might have noticed that they place you either on racing tracks or city streets where every road is as wide as a highway. Japan is known for its narrow, winding passes, extremely tight streets and even more extreme mountain corners, so this approach just wouldn’t cut it. Aiming for credibility, we wanted to recreate Japan roads as they are in reality, adding additional layers of experience to the game - one of authenticity so that roaming around our fictional Guntama feels like the real deal and one of gameplay complexity. In JDM you just won’t be able to go 200 miles per hour at all times - controlling your speed, the gear you're in and when you need to break will be as crucial as learning and understanding drifting (to cut those corners faster). We believe our game is the only title out there that provides such an experience.

Of course, we are continually working on expanding the Guntama prefecture, populating it with various, recognizable landmarks and architecture. Some are generally known to the global populace, some will have a deeper meaning for automotive fans - legendary car spots will find their way into JDM! Stay tuned next year for more precise information on the subject. For now, take a look at some examples from JDM: Rise of the Scorpion.
The Machi-no-Eki Yusuhara building might not be a hotel in-game, but it’s still a recognizable landmark, whose purpose has been tied to the story and mood aspects of JDM: Japanese Drift Master.
Haruna Lake is called Haikama Lake in JDM. See and decide for yourselves if we gave justice to this location.

Throughout the development of JDM, we strived to bring characteristic Japanese landmarks to the game and the examples above only scratch the surface of the content you will be able to uncover, as you drive around Guntama. If you’re a Japanese resident or a frequent tourist you will definitely recognise some spots. If you haven’t done so already, launch JDM: ROTS and see how many references you can find and let us know in the comments! :)

Before we close this devlog, let us say a few words about tuning, as it’s one of the most frequent subjects you ask about. It’s happening and growing by the day, both in terms of visual and technical tuning. Speaking of the latter - you will be able to buy new parts for each car. Those parts will come in tiers - each tier more expensive, but providing better performance. For as long as you can afford it, you can buy any part you want. On top of that, more advanced parts will unlock the ability to fine-tune your car's performance. We’re not ready to go into details, but expect an update focused on the subject next year.
And as for visual tuning, let the images speak for themselves:
Again, we will share more details on visual tuning with you next year.

That’s it for today. We hope you enjoyed this little summary. Tell us in the comments what made you interested in JDM in the first place. Also, don’t forget to 📌 Hit ‘Follow’ on our Steam page and add JDM: Japanese Drift Master to your wishlist to stay up-to-date on all announcements.
